The `indexing_search` tool finds code by meaning in the workspace's semantic
index. It returns chunks embedded with the configured model, merging Kilo Code's
index (when present and compatible) with this plugin's own index (Qdrant or
LanceDB). When the same chunk exists in both, the own index wins.

## When to use it

- You know the intent but not the identifiers: "user login and password
  hashing", "database connection pooling", "retry logic for failed webhooks".
- You want conceptually similar implementations across the workspace.
- You need to locate code whose name you do not know.

## When not to use it

- Exact symbol, string or error message: use Grep.
- File names or extensions: use Glob.
- A file you already know: use Read.
- Correctness that depends on the latest edit: the index can lag. Run
  `indexing_status` and `indexing_refresh`, or use Grep for certainty.

## How to call it

`indexing_search { query, path? }`

- `query` is natural language, not a symbol name. Describe what the code does.
- `path` is optional and limits results to a subdirectory, relative to the
  workspace root.
- The result limit comes from the `searchMaxResults` setting; there is no
  per-call limit.
- Each result is `file:startLine-endLine`, a similarity score and the chunk.
  Scores rank the hits of one query; they are not probabilities.
- Only files matching the configured extension allowlist are indexed. The
  default list covers common code and documentation formats; it does not
  include PowerShell `.ps1`.

## Empty or partial results

- Empty results are not proof that the code does not exist. Only indexed files
  are searchable, and a stale index can miss recent edits.
- `indexing_status` reports points, completion, freshness and the recommended
  next action. `indexing_refresh` updates incrementally; `indexing_build`
  rebuilds.
- Pausing indexing stops writes and refreshes, not reads: `indexing_search`
  still works while paused.
- With `searchKilo: false`, only the own index is searched. The tool says so
  when it finds nothing, instead of claiming Kilo has no index.

## When codegraph is also installed

The codegraph MCP server answers structure; this tool answers meaning. Use them
together:

- `indexing_search` finds the entry node by intent.
- `codegraph_explore` returns the verbatim source around it, the call paths and
  what depends on it.
- `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_impact` answer "who calls this" and "what
  breaks if I change it", which a similarity search cannot.

If codegraph is not available, the guidance above still applies and Grep remains
the fallback for exact terms.

## Configuration

`indexing_config` reports the effective settings (backend, provider/model,
credentials masked, search and behaviour). `indexing_config_set { key, value }`
changes one and persists it. Credentials are refused by design: a tool call is
recorded in the conversation. Set a key from the terminal `/indexing` page, the
Desktop settings page, the environment or the plugin options.

## Setup

Only build or import when the user asks. `indexing_build` creates the index; if
a compatible Kilo index exists and "import from Kilo" is on, vectors are copied
without embedding costs and only the delta is embedded. `indexing_import` does
the copy alone. The `/indexing` command opens the terminal settings page; on
Desktop, use Settings → Indexing.

# opencode-indexing

[![ci](https://github.com/Javierkaiser/opencode-indexing/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Javierkaiser/opencode-indexing/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](./LICENSE)
[![node: >=22.6](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22.6-brightgreen.svg)](https://nodejs.org)

OpenCode plugin that adds **semantic code search** by reusing the code index created by [Kilo Code](https://kilo.ai) and maintaining its **own independent index** (embedded LanceDB by default, or Qdrant if you prefer), so search keeps working even when Kilo isn't installed, is disabled, or its index is stale.

## TL;DR

**Why it exists.** A semantic code index is expensive to build — every chunk is
a call to an embedding API — and it only lasts as long as the tool that made it.
Kilo Code already builds one, which is worth having. But building your own means
paying for it again, and leaning on Kilo's means your search breaks the day
Kilo is uninstalled, disabled, or stale. Both are bad enough on their own.

**What it does instead.** It *reads* Kilo's index and never writes to it, then
keeps an independent index of its own next to it. Every search queries both and
merges the results, preferring whichever is fresher. If you already have a Kilo
index, its vectors are copied across **without re-embedding** — zero API calls —
and you only ever pay to index the files that changed since.

**What it is for.** Finding code by what it *does* rather than what it is
*called*, in a search that keeps working whether or not the tool that built the
index is still installed.

**Zero setup.** With no API key configured the plugin embeds locally: the package
ships a ~2 MB static model (potion-base-8M, 128 dimensions) that runs in plain
TypeScript in the same process. No network, no account, no service — and about
0.2 ms per chunk, so a full index of this repository takes seconds instead of
minutes. It is English-only; a configured cloud key still wins.

**If you never used Kilo.** `npx @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing --aio` is the
whole install: the published plugin, the codegraph companion, and a local-only
profile to match. It does not build the index — you start that when you want one.

## Install

### With npx (recommended)

```bash
npx @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing
```

This is the whole install: the installer runs `opencode plugin add`, writes the
permission rules, restarts the service, and, when you ask for it, also installs
and registers the companion `codegraph`
MCP. It picks its strategy from where it runs — from an npx cache or an
unpacked tarball it installs the published package, from a checkout it
installs your working tree instead — so edits take effect on restart with no
publish in between. It prints which one it chose.

Add `--with-codegraph` to install and register codegraph as part of the same run
(the flag is opt-in and only has effect in the published-package mode):

```bash
npx @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing --with-codegraph
```

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--aio`, `--all-in-one` | All-in-one install for a machine without Kilo: implies `--package` and `--with-codegraph`, then writes a local profile (see below) |
| `--package [spec]` | Install the published package (default spec `@latest`) |
| `--local` | Copy this directory into the config dir (development) |
| `--skip-deps` | `--local` only: copy the files, install no dependencies |
| `--no-restart` | Do not restart the service |
| `--with-codegraph` | Install and register codegraph as a companion MCP (opt-in, `--package` only) |

### All-in-one (AIO)

If Kilo was never installed, `--aio` is the install with no decisions left in it:

```bash
npx @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing --aio
```

It implies `--package` and `--with-codegraph`: it installs the published plugin,
installs and registers codegraph, and writes a local profile to
`~/.config/opencode/indexing.json`:

```json
{
  "vectorStore": "lancedb",
  "provider": "local",
  "model": "potion-multilingual-128M",
  "dimension": 256,
  "autoRefresh": false,
  "searchKilo": false,
  "importFromKilo": false
}
```

`searchKilo` and `importFromKilo` are off because there is no Kilo index to read
from or copy. `dimension: 256` is written out rather than inferred: `kilo.jsonc`
is consulted before the model registry, so a dimension left behind by Kilo would
override the multilingual model's 256. `autoRefresh: false` is the other
deliberate one — the installer does not build the index, and this keeps search
from starting one on its own. The first build is yours to start: **Settings →
Indexing → Build**, `/indexing`, or `indexing_build`.

What the install does fetch is the model. After the restart it runs the plugin's
`settings.test` for `lancedb` and `provider`; the provider test downloads the
multilingual weights (~512 MB fp32, ~123 MB int8 on first use) and confirms they
produce 256 dimensions, so the first search is not the one that discovers a
missing or broken model. `--no-restart` skips that and leaves the download to
first use.

Existing keys and credentials in `indexing.json` are preserved: the profile is
merged into the file, not written over it, and a file that is not valid JSON is
left untouched with a warning. Plugin `options` in `opencode.json` still win over
the file, so an option that sets one of these keys takes precedence and the
installer says so. `--aio` is the published-package install and cannot be
combined with `--local`.

Running `--aio` again is safe. If the plugin is already installed — a `plugins`
entry in `opencode.json`, the copy at
`<config>/opencode/plugins/opencode-indexing`, a `javierkaiser.indexing` line in
`opencode plugin list` — or `indexing.json` already exists, the installer
applies no profile: it says what it found, leaves the file untouched, and skips
the `settings.test` model prefetch, so the multilingual weights are not
downloaded a second time. The rest of the install still runs: plugin
add/update, the codegraph registration, the permission rules and the service
restart.

If the plugin is already installed, change the profile from **Settings →
Indexing**; re-running the installer will not replace it. If only an
`indexing.json` exists (the plugin is not detected), back it up, remove it, and
run `--aio` again: with no file to protect, the installer writes the profile and
fetches the model.

### The codegraph companion

[CodeGraph](https://github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph) is a separate tool — a
local code-graph indexer exposed as an MCP server — and this plugin drives it
rather than reimplementing it. If it is not installed yet:

```bash
npm install -g @colbymchenry/codegraph
```

The package is scoped, and that matters: `codegraph` unscoped on npm is an
unrelated 2024 library with no CLI, so installing that name exits 0 and leaves
nothing on `PATH`.

Installing it is only half of it. `indexing_build` and `indexing_import` also
start the CLI for the workspace, so both indexes are built by the same action:
`codegraph init --yes` the first time a folder is seen, `codegraph sync`
afterwards. codegraph is a **companion, not a dependency** — with the CLI absent
nothing is spawned, no build fails, and no line is added to the output. Turn it
off with `/indexing-config set codegraph=false`, and see
[Semantic search and code graphs](#semantic-search-and-code-graphs) for why the
two belong together.

The launch is detached and reported as started, never as finished: on a large
monorepo `init` runs for minutes, and a tool call that blocked that long would
be worse than one that returns. Anything that fails afterwards lands in
`.codegraph/daemon.log`. A home directory or a drive root is refused rather than
indexed, and launches are limited to one per 15 seconds per workspace because
codegraph's own daemon already watches files.

### With the OpenCode CLI

```bash
opencode plugin add @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing
```

OpenCode downloads the package into its own cache and records it in the global
`plugins` array, and the host loads the parts the client runs: the server side
(`index.ts`, which registers the tools), the terminal UI (`tui.ts`, which adds
the prompt-footer indicator and the `/indexing` page), and — in OpenCode
Desktop — the GUI part (`dist/gui-experimental.cjs`, which adds the settings
page, palette commands and composer pill). It brings `plugin check`, `plugin
update` and `plugin remove` with it, but it cannot write permission rules — add
this one to `opencode.json` to keep the host asking before the only tool that
writes your settings file:

```jsonc
{
  "permissions": [
    { "action": "indexing_config_set", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }
  ]
}
```

The other six tools only read. OpenCode's base policy already allows everything
(`{ "action": "*", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" }`), so they need no rule;
write them out only if you want to tighten the set.

`install.sh` and `install.ps1` are thin wrappers over it; PowerShell also accepts
`-Aio`, `-Local`, `-Package`, `-Spec`, `-SkipDeps`, `-NoRestart` and
`-WithCodegraph`.

`--package` deletes any copied plugin it finds: both sources define the same
plugin id (`javierkaiser.indexing`) and the config directory is scanned
automatically, so leaving both would load the plugin twice.

If no package manager is available, a `--local` install still copies the files
and the plugin runs with reduced features (line chunker instead of tree-sitter,
no LanceDB).

### Upgrading from 0.5.x

0.6.0 changes the plugin id from `opencode.indexing` to
`javierkaiser.indexing`, because OpenCode reserves the `opencode` namespace for
its own plugins. The host stores this plugin's file manifest under its plugin
id, so the manifest written by 0.5.x is not visible to 0.6.0. The own index is
reindexed once: the workspace is rescanned and every indexed file is embedded
again. No vectors are deleted, and Kilo's index is untouched; with the bundled
local model no API calls are involved, while a cloud provider bills one full
embedding run. The TUI command ids (`opencode.indexing.settings`, `.dialogs`,
`.toggle`, …) keep their old prefix: they are a keybinding contract independent
of the plugin id, so existing `cli.json` bindings keep working.

### Manual

To manage the directory yourself, point `opencode.json` at it. Relative paths
resolve from the config file containing the entry:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": ["./plugins/opencode-indexing"]
}
```

## How it works

```
OpenCode ──► indexing_search ──┬──► Kilo's index (read-only)      Qdrant ws-*  ·  Kilo LanceDB
                               └──► own index (read/write)        own LanceDB (default)  ·  Qdrant oc-*

OpenCode ──► codegraph_*  ───────► codegraph's graph (its own)    .codegraph/codegraph.db
             ▲
             └── indexing_build / indexing_import keep it in step
```

- **Read-only reuse**: the plugin computes the same collection name Kilo uses (`ws-` + sha256 of the workspace path, first 16 hex chars), validates the embedding profile stored in the metadata point, and queries with an embedding from the *same* model (e.g. Mistral `codestral-embed-2505`, 1536d).
- **Import without re-embedding**: `indexing_build` (or `indexing_import`) can copy vectors + chunks from an existing Kilo index — both its Qdrant collections and its local LanceDB database — at **zero embedding cost**, then incrementally index only the delta.
- **Own index**: manifest-based incremental indexer (per-file sha256) writing to `oc-*` collections or an embedded LanceDB database, using the same chunk payload shape as Kilo (`filePath`, `fileHash`, `codeChunk`, `startLine`, `endLine`, `segmentHash`, `pathSegments`).
- **Merge**: results from Kilo + own are merged; own (fresher) hits win on overlap; ghost hits (deleted files) are filtered out.
- **Companion graph**: the same build starts codegraph for the workspace, which keeps its own index in `.codegraph/` and serves it over its own MCP server. This plugin never reads or writes that database — see [Semantic search and code graphs](#semantic-search-and-code-graphs).

## Tools (namespace `indexing`)

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `indexing_search` | Semantic search across Kilo's index + own index. `{ query, path? }`. Ends with a one-line index status |
| `indexing_status` | Backends, Kilo sources available for import, both indexes, freshness, recommendation |
| `indexing_config` | Effective configuration: backend, provider/model, credentials (masked), search and behavior settings, settings file, Kilo sources. Read-only |
| `indexing_config_set` | Change one setting and persist it. `{ key, value }`. Refuses credentials |
| `indexing_refresh` | Incremental update of the own index (new/changed/deleted files only) |
| `indexing_build` | Build the own index: imports from Kilo when compatible, otherwise embeds from scratch. `{ rebuild?, skipImport? }` |
| `indexing_import` | Import a specific Kilo source without re-embedding. `{ source?, rebuild? }`; `rebuild` drops the own index first |

### Bundled skill

The plugin registers a skill, `opencode-indexing` ("Semantic code search
(indexing)"), that tells the model when `indexing_search` is the right tool,
when Grep, Glob or Read are the better ones, how to read empty results, and how
to keep the index fresh. It ships as `skills/opencode-indexing/SKILL.md` and is
registered from that file, so there is nothing to install. Mention it as
`@opencode-indexing`, or let the model load it when the description matches.

## Settings

The terminal page and its dialog editor write the same file through the server
plugin's RPC; `/indexing-config set` writes it from the server. The Desktop
settings page writes it too: provider and model from the catalog, vector store,
credentials, search limits and the booleans, plus a one-click local setup. The
`indexing_config` tool reports the configuration without writing it, and refuses
credentials because a tool call is recorded in the conversation.

### `/indexing-config` — slash command

Registered as a server command, so the host lists it in every client. Whether typing it *runs* it depends on the client: the terminal TUI and the Desktop app submit the line to the model instead of dispatching the command, so there it does nothing. To read the configuration from those, ask the assistant — it calls `indexing_config`, which returns the same report — or, in Desktop, open the plugin's settings page. The subcommands below apply wherever the command is dispatched.

| Subcommand | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/indexing-config` or `show` | Print the effective configuration and any warnings |
| `/indexing-config set <key>=<value>` | Change one setting. `set <key>` alone prints its current value; `set <key>=reset` reverts it |
| `/indexing-config test [target]` | Test connectivity: `qdrant`, `lancedb`, `provider`, `kilo` |
| `/indexing-config import [source]` | Import vectors from a Kilo source without re-embedding |
| `/indexing-config help` | List keys and subcommands |

Settable keys (case-insensitive):

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `vectorstore` | `qdrant` or `lancedb` |
| `qdranturl` / `qdrantapikey` | Qdrant connection |
| `lancedbdirectory` | LanceDB directory for the own index |
| `provider` / `model` | Embedding provider and model |
| `mistralkey` / `openaikey` / `geminikey` / `voyagekey` / `openrouterkey` | API keys for those providers |
| `ollamaurl` | Ollama base URL |
| `openaicompatibleurl` / `openaicompatiblekey` | OpenAI-compatible endpoint |
| `importfromkilo` | `true` to import from Kilo when building, `false` to start from scratch |
| `codegraph` | `false` to stop also running the `codegraph` CLI on build. On by default; a no-op when codegraph is not installed |
| `autorefresh` | Refresh the own index automatically on search |
| `enabled` | Master switch. `false` pauses writing and refreshing; search keeps working, and still reads Kilo's index unless `searchKilo` is off |
| `searchmaxresults` | Result cap per search |
| `embeddingbatchsize` | Embedding batch size |
| `searchminscore` | Minimum similarity score |
| `fileextensions` | Extensions to index |

### `/indexing` — settings page (terminal TUI)

Opens a full settings page: current configuration, 
…[文件过长——仅保留首 16KB 与末 8KB]…
s plugin never writes to:

| Index | Default | Configured by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Own index | embedded LanceDB, under `~/.local/state/opencode-indexing/lancedb` | `vectorStore` |
| Kilo index (read-only) | whatever `kilo.jsonc` says | Kilo itself |
| codegraph's graph | `.codegraph/` inside the workspace | codegraph itself |

Kilo's `vectorStore` used to decide where this plugin's own index was written,
because both were read from the same setting chain. That is no longer the case:
Kilo decides where an import **reads from**, and your own index decides where it
**writes to**. If Kilo is on Qdrant and you have not set `vectorStore` yourself,
the own index still goes to LanceDB and `indexing_status` says so.

### Platform support for the embedded store

`@lancedb/lancedb` 0.40.0 is a JavaScript wrapper around a native library, with
one prebuilt binary per platform and no WebAssembly fallback. The platforms it
ships a binary for are:

| Platform | `platform-arch` | Own index on LanceDB |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows x64 / arm64 | `win32-x64`, `win32-arm64` | yes |
| Linux x64 / arm64 (glibc and musl) | `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64` | yes |
| macOS Apple Silicon | `darwin-arm64` | yes |
| **macOS Intel** | `darwin-x64` | **no binary is published** |

On macOS Intel the default store cannot load, and installing it again will not
help. The plugin says so explicitly and asks you to pick Qdrant:

```
LanceDB is the default store for the own index but has no native binary for
darwin-x64. It cannot run on this platform and reinstalling will not change
that. Set vectorStore=qdrant explicitly in
~/.config/opencode/indexing.json to use a Qdrant server instead.
```

Set `vectorStore=qdrant` in `~/.config/opencode/indexing.json` (or run
`/indexing-config set vectorstore=qdrant`) to use a Qdrant server instead.

## Semantic search and code graphs

Two indexes, not two options. This plugin builds and searches the semantic one;
it also keeps codegraph's code graph in step for the same folder, so a single
`indexing_build` leaves both current. Neither replaces the other, and this is not
a fork of codegraph — see [The codegraph companion](#the-codegraph-companion)
for the install side.

### The two indexes

| | Semantic index (this plugin) | Code graph (codegraph) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Question it answers | "Where is the code that does something like X?" | "Who calls X? What breaks if I change it? Path from A to B?" |
| Signal | Meaning (embeddings over chunks) | Structure (symbols, `CALLS`, `DEFINES`, `IMPORTS` edges) |
| Strengths | Natural language, concepts without known identifiers, cross-language | Exact structural facts, multi-hop traversals, no similarity false positives |
| Weaknesses | "Similar" is not "relevant"; no notion of connections | Cannot find a concept with no known symbol; fragile on dynamic code |
| What it costs to stay fresh | **Paid**: the embedding API, re-run when the model changes | **Free**: local parsing and a small graph store, re-run on every edit |

That last row is what shapes the setup. A semantic index is re-embedded only when
the model changes, and that is money; a graph is synced whenever a file is
touched, and that is CPU. Two cadences for two economies — which is the reason
to keep both pointed at one folder rather than at two projects that quietly
drift apart.

### Measuring the difference

We measured this rather than assuming it. [`bench/`](./bench) runs the same
real questions about code through four methods — word matching, symbol-name
lookup, this plugin's semantic search, and a fusion of the last two — over two
codebases of different languages, and counts how often each finds the right
file. The [report](./bench/results.md) opens with the numbers in plain language.
What it found:

- **Symbol-name lookup was the weakest of the four**, in both codebases. It only
  matches what things are *called*, so a question in ordinary words has little to
  grab onto.
- **Semantic search and plain word matching traded places.** On one codebase
  semantic won clearly (100% vs 76% found in the top 10); on the other they were
  close (60% vs 55%). Neither replaces the other.
- **Fusing semantic with symbol lookup was never worse than semantic alone**, and
  better on both: more files found on one codebase, a better position on the
  other.

One caveat, and it is larger than it looks. The benchmark measures
`codegraph query`, the one subcommand that matches **names**. It does **not**
measure what a graph is actually good for — who calls what, what breaks if you
change it, paths between two places. So the fusion above is *semantic + name
matching*, **not** *semantic + graph traversal*. What would actually justify
reaching for the graph is not in those numbers, and this section does not claim
it is.

### Using them together

The division of labour is the one the wider field converges on: use embeddings
to find the entry node **by intent**, then walk the graph for **exact
relationships**.

1. `indexing_search` — "where is the retry logic for failed webhooks". Finds the
   neighbourhood from meaning alone, with no identifier to know in advance.
2. `codegraph_explore` — the same area, returning the verbatim source of the
   relevant symbols, the call paths between them, and what depends on them.
3. `codegraph_impact` / `codegraph_callers` — once the question becomes "what
   breaks if I change this", the graph answers exactly, and a similarity search
   cannot.

Both are live in the same session, so an assistant moves between them without
being asked to.

### Why there are no graph tools in this plugin

There are no `indexing_graph_*` tools here, and that is a decision rather than a
gap. An earlier version of this section proposed adding tree-sitter symbol and
edge extraction into SQLite as a candidate for a future major version. Once
codegraph was available as a companion, that plan would have reimplemented
something another tool already does better — in a second store, behind a second
indexer that has to be kept alive and fresh.

The plugin stays on the semantic side and coexists with grep/read (see the tool
descriptions and the bundled skill). What it adds for the structural half is to
keep it current, not to duplicate it.

## Development

```powershell
npm install
node --test "test/*.test.ts"   # unit tests (Node 26 runs TS natively)

# CLI harness against the real environment:
node test/cli.ts status     --root .
node test/cli.ts search "database connection pooling" --root .
node test/cli.ts build      --root .            # import from Kilo when possible
node test/cli.ts import     --root . --source ws-43dfc9b3ee33fcfd
node test/cli.ts build      --vector-store lancedb --root .
```

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [0.10.2] - 2026-11-10

### Fixed
- **The re-run guard no longer tells an installed user to delete
  `indexing.json`.** With the plugin installed, the other half of the guard
  would still skip, so that instruction went in circles. The message now points
  at Settings → Indexing, and the README distinguishes an installed plugin from
  a settings file without one: only the latter can be removed and re-run to
  apply the profile.

## [0.10.1] - 2026-11-10

### Changed
- **Re-running `--aio` no longer replaces an existing provider, model or store.**
  It re-applied the all-in-one profile and re-ran the model prefetch on every
  run, so a machine already set up with another provider, model or vector store
  was moved back to the local profile by a command that reads as an update. When
  the plugin is already installed — a `plugins` entry in `opencode.json`, the
  copy at `<config>/opencode/plugins/opencode-indexing`, the package in
  `opencode plugin list` — or `indexing.json` already exists, the installer now
  reports what it found, leaves the file untouched, and skips the model
  prefetch. The idempotent steps still run: plugin add/update, codegraph
  registration, the permission rules and the service restart. To apply the
  profile deliberately, back up and remove `indexing.json` and run `--aio`
  again.

## [0.10.0] - 2026-11-10

### Added
- **`--aio` / `--all-in-one` is the install for a machine that never ran Kilo.**
  It implies `--package` and `--with-codegraph`, so one command installs the
  published plugin and the codegraph companion, and then writes a local-only
  profile to `~/.config/opencode/indexing.json`: embedded LanceDB, the
  multilingual static model at 256 dimensions, no Kilo search, no import from
  Kilo and no auto-refresh. `dimension` is written out because `kilo.jsonc` is
  consulted before the model registry, so a dimension left behind by Kilo would
  otherwise override the model's 256; `autoRefresh: false` because the installer
  does not build the index - that stays a decision the user makes from Settings,
  `/indexing` or `indexing_build`. The model is downloaded and validated at
  install time (~512 MB fp32, ~123 MB after quantization) by running the
  plugin's own `settings.test` for `lancedb` and `provider`, which also confirms
  the 256 dimensions; `--no-restart` skips that. Existing keys and credentials in
  `indexing.json` are preserved, a file that is not valid JSON is left untouched
  with a warning, and a plugin option that sets one of the profile keys still
  wins over the file. `--aio` cannot be combined with `--local`, and both
  wrappers forward it (`-Aio` in PowerShell).

## [0.9.0] - 2026-11-10

### Changed
- **The Desktop composer pill shows the index state, not the point count.**
  "2.2k points" answered how big the index was, not whether it could be used,
  and the number is one click away in Settings. The pill now reads `indexed`,
  `index stale`, `not indexed`, `paused`, `indexing…`, `reading…`, `no index`
  or `index error` - the same vocabulary as the terminal footer and the chat
  line, so the same state never reads differently in two places.
- **The bundled skill moved to `skills/opencode-indexing/SKILL.md`.** It used
  to be a string inside `index.ts`, registered with an
  `opencode-indexing://skill/indexing` path that is not a file: the host could
  not give it a real base directory or list supporting files. The server
  registers the real file now, and `files` ships it. The content also documents
  the `path` argument, that the limit comes from `searchMaxResults`, that
  search keeps working while indexing is paused, what `searchKilo: false`
  changes, and that `.ps1` is outside the default extension allowlist.

## [0.8.0] - 2026-11-10

### Added
- **`ownStoreReachable` is part of the `status.get` output contract.** The
  server has computed it since the footer needed to tell an unreachable store
  from an index that simply does not exist yet, and the TUI and the GUI already
  read it, but the declared schema never listed it: it survived only because the
  schema allows additional properties, so a consumer validating against the
  definition could not see it. It is declared now.

### Changed
- **The dev toolchain moves to OpenCode 2.2.7.** `@opencode/plugin` and
  `@opencode/theme` are pinned to exactly 2.2.7 in devDependencies, and the
  consumer peers are `@opencode/plugin >=2.2.7` and `solid-js >=1.9.0`, both
  still optional. The floor comes from the Desktop page: it is built from the
  settings components OpenCode 2.2.6 added, so an older host cannot render it.
  The pins are exact because the SDK the typecheck sees has to be the one the
  page's components come from.
- **`@opencode/theme` and `@opentui/*` are no longer consumer peers.** The TUI
  is JSX-free and imports the host runtime through virtual module ids, so
  OpenTUI is needed only to typecheck those declarations — a devDependency, not
  something a consumer installs. The theme is provided by the host and pinned by
  the SDK. Peers that the package never loads itself only ask users to resolve
  dependencies it does not use.
- **The Desktop settings page is rebuilt on the host's own components.**
  `SettingsLayout`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingsRow` and `Select` replace the
  hand-rolled layout that copied the host's measurements and coloured itself
  from `--v2-*`. A copied number is a snapshot of one release and drifts
  silently; the components cannot drift from the host they come from, so the
  page follows its theme and layout by construction.

### Fixed
- **`searchKilo: false` is no longer reported as a missing Kilo index.**
  `indexing_status` now says that Kilo search is disabled instead of reusing the
  "no Kilo index" text, `indexing_search` says only the own index was searched
  when it finds nothing, and the paused line in `indexing_config` says search
  reads the own index only. The two states need different actions — a switch
  versus a build — and the old wording sent readers to the wrong one. The "Set
  up locally" preset also stopped writing `searchKilo: true`, so it no longer
  overrides a choice the user made.
- **The LanceDB install hint no longer names 0.26.2.** The package has shipped
  `@lancedb/lancedb` 0.40.0 since 0.3.2, but the message shown when the module
  is missing still told people to install 0.26.2 — a downgrade of the native
  binary the code is written against. It names 0.40.0 now.
- **The `index.import` RPC no longer declares a `rebuild` input that nothing
  reads.** The schema offered it and the handler ignored it, so a caller who
  passed it believed the index had been dropped and rebuilt. It is gone. The
  `indexing_build` and `indexing_import` tools keep their own `rebuild`, which
  is honored.

## [0.7.3] - 2026-11-03

### Fixed
- **The Desktop settings page was missing the `searchKilo` switch** added in
  0.7.2. The TUI page and the dialog editor had it; the GUI — which is where a
  Desktop user looks — still offered only "Import from Kilo", so the setting was
  unreachable from there.

## [0.7.2] - 2026-11-03

### Added
- **`searchKilo`, so a local index stays searchable next to an unusable Kilo
  one.** Search reads both indexes and refuses to answer when one of them holds
  points built with a profile this machine cannot embed — an expired cloud key or
  an exhausted budget. That refusal is right (a half answer looks complete), but
  it left the own index unreachable too. With `searchKilo: false`
  (`KILO_INDEX_SEARCH_KILO=false`, or the new switch in the settings page and the
  dialog menu) the search uses the own index only, without querying Qdrant for
  Kilo's collection at all.

  Wired through the whole surface: settings file, plugin options, environment,
  `indexing_config`, the TUI page, the dialog editor and the RPC view.

### Documentation
- The README explains when turning Kilo's index off is the right move.

## [0.7.1] - 2026-11-02

### Fixed
- The `indexing_config_set` description and the bundled skill still said the
  settings file never stores keys in plain text, and pointed only at the
  environment or plugin options. Keys can be typed in the TUI and the Desktop
  page; both messages now say so, and still refuse credentials on a tool call.
- The `indexing_config` description now points at `indexing_config_set` and the
  settings surfaces, instead of only the slash command and the file.
- The README's surface list said “all three terminal surfaces”; it now lists the
  four, including the Desktop page, and the duplicated “model is chosen from a
  catalog” sentence is gone.

## [0.7.0] - 2026-11-02

### Added
- **The Desktop settings page configures everything.** It was a read-only report
  with three switches. It now edits the embedding provider and model from the
  server's catalog, the vector store and its locations, the API keys, the search
  limits and the indexing switches, all through the host's own controls and
  dialogs.
- **A one-click local setup.** “Set up locally” checks LanceDB, selects the
  bundled local model and embedded LanceDB, turns on import-from-Kilo and
  auto-refresh, and runs the first build. No key, no server, one reindex.
- `catalog.get`, `settings.apply` and `settings.credential` RPC methods. The
  catalog is served rather than imported because `src/registry.ts` imports
  `node:crypto` and the GUI runs in the renderer, with no Node built-ins.
- `settings.get` now reports `codegraph`, `searchMinScore`,
  `embeddingBatchSize`, `fileExtensions`, `kiloVectorStore` and `warnings`, so
  the page can show and edit them.

### Changed
- **Credentials are editable from the settings surfaces.** The TUI already wrote
  keys to `indexing.json`; the Desktop page now does too, through a native
  secret prompt and its own `settings.credential` method. The chat tool still
  refuses them, because a tool call is recorded in the conversation.
- The README said API keys were never written to `indexing.json` in plain text.
  That was false: the TUI has always written them. It now states what happens,
  and recommends the environment or plugin options for anyone who does not want
  them in that file.

### Fixed
- The credential-refusal message repeated the same false claim. It now points to
  the surfaces where a key can be typed.

## [0.6.3] - 2026-11-02

### Fixed
- **The Desktop page did not match the host's measurements.** The previous
  version invented a header inside the card and sized its rows by eye, which is
  why it still read as a neighbouring app rather than the same one. The values
  now come from the app's own settings CSS: a 720px column, 48px above the page
  title, lists with a layer-01 background and a half-pixel inset border, rows
  with 20px of vertical padding and a half-pixel separator, a 15px/640 page
  title and 13px/530 row titles. The section title moved above its list, where
  the host puts it, instead of living inside it.
- **Colours come from the app's theme variables** (`--v2-*`) rather than a grey
  mixed from `currentColor`. The variables are the ones the host itself uses, so
  light and dark follow exactly instead of approximately.
- The three switch rows carry the host's title-plus-description layout, which is
  also what gives them the height the other settings rows have.

## [0.6.2] - 2026-11-02

### Changed
- **The Desktop settings page looks like the rest of the app.** It was drawing
  its own buttons, borders and typography, which is why it read as a different
  application next to Pairing or Projects. The page now has a title and
  subtitle, cards with a section header and separated rows, and uses the host's
  own controls: `ctx.ui.Button`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Loader`, `Icon` and
  `Switch`. The SDK exposes no theme tokens, so the layout stays ours and every
  border is mixed from `currentColor`, which follows the host's light and dark
  themes instead of hardcoding a grey.

- **Indexing enabled, Import from Kilo and Auto refresh are now editable from
  Desktop.** They are the three booleans, so they use the host's switch rather
  than a checkbox that only exists here. Each write goes through
  `settings.set`, and the page adopts the settings the server returns rather
  than the value it asked for: a clamped or rejected change cannot look accepted
  until the next reload. A failed write shows a toast and leaves the switch on
  the stored value.

### Added
- Two tests pin the presentation: the page uses the host's components and
  contains no raw `<button>`, and the three booleans are wired to `settings.set`
  with the server's answer adopted through `mutate`.

## [0.6.1] - 2026-11-02

### Fixed
- **The Desktop settings page rendered blank.** It asked `status.get` for a
  freshness check. A settings page has no session, so the request carried no
  directory and the server scanned its own — on a service started from a home
  directory, that is the whole machine. The scan outlived the RPC transport
  timeout, the promise rejected, and the page had nothing left to render. The
  read is now the cheap one: freshness belongs to the index actions, not to
  opening a page.

- **A failed read shows its reason instead of producing a blank page.** The
  resource resolves with `{ error }` rather than rejecting, and the page renders
  that reason with a Reload button. A rejected resource has nothing to render,
  which is how the bug above stayed invisible long enough to ship.

- **The page takes the setup context as a prop.** It called `usePlugin`, which
  throws outside the host's provider; the SDK documents that provider for
  routes, dialogs and slots, not for settings pages. Whether the host wraps this
  page was an assumption, and it did not need to be one.

### Added
- Three tests pin those three properties by reading the source, because each is
  invisible to the typecheck and only fails at runtime inside the app.

## [0.6.0] - 2026-11-02

### Added
- **An OpenCode Desktop GUI part.** The package now exports
  `./gui-experimental` as one prebuilt CommonJS file,
  `dist/gui-experimental.cjs`, built with Vite from `src/gui.tsx` and the
  `@opencode/plugin/gui` SDK. Desktop loads it beside the server and TUI parts
  and gets three surfaces: a settings page that reports the plugin's
  configuration read-only, with Build and Refresh actions, palette commands for
  those two index actions, and a composer pill for index state. The TUI footer
  stays terminal-only; the composer pill is how the same state reaches Desktop.

  This is also the package's fourth V2 part. The same npm package now exports
  `.` (server), `./tui`, `./gui-experimental` and `./rpc`, and the host loads
  the parts a given client needs. The build tools are `devDependencies`: the
  published package ships the bundle, not Vite, vite-plugin-solid or SolidJS.

### Changed
- **The plugin id is `javierkaiser.indexing`, not `opencode.indexing`.** OpenCode
  reserves the `opencode` namespace for its own plugin ids, and a plugin id in
  that namespace prevents OpenCode Desktop from loading the plugin's GUI at all:
  keeping the old id would have kept the new Desktop part from appearing, no
  matter what the package exported. The package name, tool namespace and
  settings file are unchanged.

  The id is also the host storage namespace, so the file manifest written under
  `opencode.indexing` is not visible under `javierkaiser.indexing`. On first use
  after upgrading, the own index is reindexed once: the workspace is rescanned
  and every indexed file is embedded again. No vectors are deleted, and Kilo's
  index is untouched. With the bundled local model the pass makes no API calls;
  with a cloud provider it is one full embedding run.

  The TUI command ids still begin with `opencode.indexing` (`settings`,
  `dialogs`, `toggle` and the page keys). They are a keybinding contract
  independent of the plugin id, and renaming them would break existing
  `cli.json` bindings. The new Desktop commands are published as
  `javierkaiser.indexing.build` and `.refresh`; they had no earlier id to
  preserve.

- **Developm

og at all. `indexing_config` lists every model with its dimension and
  whether Kilo also knows it — which is the whole answer to whether a free import
  will work.
- **Per-model input ceilings and per-provider batch limits.** The ceilings differ by
  more than an order of magnitude (`mxbai-embed-large` takes 512 tokens,
  `voyage-code-4` takes 32,000), and one global constant truncated every chunk past
  the smallest model's limit. Batch limits are now per provider: OpenAI caps a
  request at 300,000 tokens whatever the item count, Gemini accepts a fixed number of
  items, Voyage has both.
- `voyage-code-4`, `voyage-4`, `voyage-4-large`, `voyage-4-lite`,
  `gemini-embedding-2` and Ollama's `bge-m3` in the catalog, each marked as not
  present in Kilo's registry so it is clear they cannot be imported.
- `indexing_status` warns before a model change re-embeds the workspace, with the
  point count, rather than after the embeddings have been paid for.

### Changed

- **A search that cannot read part of the corpus now fails instead of shrinking.**
  An embedding failure per profile was pushed onto a list rendered as "Warnings", and
  the results that came back looked exactly like a complete set whose missing half
  ranked lower. An index holding points whose profile cannot be embedded is now an
  error naming the profile. An index with no points is not an error, so the common
  case is unaffected.
- Changing provider clears the model, because model ids are namespaced per provider.
  The previous code claimed to do this and did not, so switching to Voyage produced
  `voyage` + `codestral-embed-2505`, which outranks the provider default.
- The stored dimension of a previous index is no longer inherited across a provider
  change. A 1536-wide Mistral index made any new model look 1536-dimensional, and the
  inherited number was then persisted as though it had been measured, making the
  mismatch self-consistent and invisible on every later run.
- The `apiKeys` merge is derived from the incoming keys instead of a hand-written list
  of provider names, which silently dropped any credential added to the shape but not
  to the list.
- The settings page reports which providers have credentials instead of deriving it
  from two booleans, which reported "none configured" for a Gemini, Voyage,
  OpenRouter, Ollama or OpenAI-compatible setup.
- `indexing_config` and `settings test kilo` pass a target profile to the Kilo source
  scan. Without it every source was reported as compatible, including ones that would
  be refused a moment later.
- Ollama and Voyage are sent `truncate` / `truncation: false`, so an over-long chunk
  fails instead of being silently shortened into a valid-looking wrong vector.
- Embedding results are placed by `data[].index` where the provider supplies it.
  OpenAI documents the field rather than promising response order, and its own samples
  fetch by it; a repeated or out-of-range index is now an error.
- The catalog's `openrouter` Gemini entry names `google/gemini-embedding-2-preview`,
  which is what Kilo writes. It said `google/gemini-embedding-001`, and since the
  profile comparison is exact string equality the drift was invisible and made every
  such index un-importable.

### Fixed

- The model field is cleared on a provider change in the TUI as well as the chat
  command; both paths had the same stale-model bug.
- `searchCode` and `getStatus` had no unit tests — only the e2e and cli scripts
  exercised them, and those assert nothing. Both have tests now.

### Documentation

- The README states how far each provider has actually been tested. `mistral` has
  touched its real API; `openrouter` reached the API and authenticated but was
  refused by the key's own spend limit; `openai`, `gemini`, `voyage`,
  `openai-compatible` and `ollama` have never contacted a real endpoint and are
  covered only by fixtures written alongside their adapters. The same fact is
  surfaced in the model chooser and in `indexing_config`, and a test pins the list so
  the claim cannot quietly widen.

## [0.1.1] - 2026-10-14

### Added

- `src/lancedb-support.ts` reports up front that LanceDB ships one native binary per
  platform and that there is no `lancedb-darwin-x64` build (there is no WASM
  fallback), so the embedded store is unavailable on macOS on Intel — instead of
  failing later with a module-not-found error.

### Changed

- **The own index now defaults to embedded LanceDB** instead of inheriting Kilo's
  `vectorStore`. Kilo's setting is read as `kiloVectorStore`: it still decides where
  an *import* reads from, and it is still reported, but it no longer decides where
  the own index writes to. Dropping that inheritance is reported as a warning rather
  than applied silently, so an existing Qdrant own index is not discovered to be
  empty.
- npm releases are now automated: pushing a `v*` tag triggers a GitHub Actions
  workflow that publishes through npm trusted publishing (OIDC), with no
  long-lived token.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-09

First public release.

### Added

- `indexing_search`, `indexing_status`, `indexing_refresh`, `indexing_build` and
  `indexing_import` tools.
- Read-only reuse of Kilo Code indexes (Qdrant `ws-*` collections and Kilo's
  local LanceDB database).
- Import of Kilo vectors and chunks at zero embedding cost, with an incremental
  delta after the import.
- Own index (Qdrant `oc-*` collections or embedded LanceDB) with a
  manifest-based incremental indexer keyed on per-file SHA-256.
- Results from Kilo and the own index merged, with fresher own hits winning on
  overlap and ghost hits filtered out.
- `/indexing-config` server command (works in terminal, Desktop and web) and the
  `/indexing` terminal settings page.
- Prompt-footer index status indicator.
- Cross-platform installer (`install.mjs`, plus `install.sh` / `install.ps1`
  wrappers).
